findings.title: Wrong release-note text passes the audit
findings.description: `auditNotes()` compares rendered entries with grouped entries using only their source SHAs and commit URLs, without comparing their subjects or other note content. If rendering swaps or removes subjects while preserving the sources and counts, all five checks can pass even though the displayed notes describe the wrong commits.

findings.title: Misclassified notes pass the audit
findings.description: `auditNotes()` flattens the grouped and JSON sections before comparing SHAs, while its Markdown check ignores section headings. If rendering moves an entry into another section without changing the overall entry order, the audit passes despite the release notes assigning that commit to the wrong category.

findings.title: Unrelated Day 12 journal edit ships in this PR
findings.description: The diff changes `journal/day-12.md`: it rewrites the PR 28 status line to "Merged by the human as `3903f33`" and adds a discussion-post link. The author notes say this file holds the human's unrelated uncommitted edit and is not part of this change, so the T-032 commit now carries Day 12 journal content that nobody reviewed as part of the ticket.

findings.title: A helper's comment describes two functions
findings.description: The doc comment above `difference` says it returns items of `a` not in `b` *and* items that occur more than once in `a`, but `difference` only filters by membership; the duplicate part belongs to the separate `duplicates` function below it. Someone reading `difference(...)` calls in the checks (for example `missing`, `mdExtra`) may believe they already catch repeats, and may drop the explicit `duplicates(...)` calls that `exactly-once` and `markdown-links` depend on.

findings.title: Valid Git ranges are rejected
findings.description: Step 1 appends `^{commit}` to the entire input, so a valid Git expression such as `HEAD^!` is reported as unresolved. When someone supplies that expression, the procedure tells them to stop even though `git rev-list` can enumerate its commits.

findings.title: A moved pull request can pass the gate
findings.description: The gate procedure checks whether `headRefOid` moved only after its second PR read, then queries checks and review state without revalidating that head before declaring `MET`. If a commit is pushed during those later steps, the report can describe green checks and a completed review for an earlier head while the live pull request contains different code.

findings.title: Dismissed findings get invalid decisions
findings.description: The gate report maps a dismissed finding's `decision` to its stored `dismiss_reason` rather than to one of the decisions specified in `AGENTS.md`. When a finding is dismissed, that reason can appear in the decision column instead of a valid gate decision, leaving the report's required disposition unclear.

findings.title: Merge commits hide code changes from the gate
findings.description: Step 4 of pr-gate-check lists files with `git log --format="commit %H" --name-only "$R..$HEAD"`. By default `git log` prints no diff for a merge commit, so a merge after the reviewed commit gets a `commit` line and no file list. If that merge's conflict resolution edits `src/` or `.ts` files, the step lists no such file, and the docs-only allowance can report the gate MET for code no review has seen.

findings.title: Commit links in a subject fail a clean audit
findings.description: `markdown-links` uses `linkRe` and `anyCommitLink` to scan an entire entry line for `](`, so they also count commit-link-shaped text in a subject after `escapeText` turns its closing bracket into `\]`. When a conventional commit subject contains text such as `[abc1234](https://example.com/commit/<40-hex-sha>)`, the renderer places that escaped text before the real source link, and the audit reports FAIL despite there being only one active commit link.

findings.title: The real-range audit run is not saved with the PR
findings.description: The PR adds the release-notes-audit skill and its tests, but no saved audit output for a real repository range is in the diff. The only evidence under `evidence/day13/` is a test run and a `check` run, and neither is an audit of a range; the skill's required `audit.txt`, `notes.json`, `group.json` and the other evidence files are absent. The PR author's notes say the fresh-session run is deferred until after the merge, so this is a planned gap rather than an oversight, but the verification criterion is still unmet at the point this PR is reviewed. Until that run is saved, the skill has only been dry-run from the drafting session, and those dry-run results are not stored as evidence.

review_agent_comment: The audit procedure is clear, but the range-validation step appears narrower than the range inputs it advertises. Could you align the validation with the supported inputs?
